subsystems.name: Drill and sample core
subsystems.role: interrogates rock up to 2 m beneath the surface, below the layer where radiation and oxidants destroy organic molecules.

subsystems.name: Sample handling and sealed laboratory
subsystems.role: moves each core without contamination into instruments that analyse it internally.

subsystems.name: Pasteur analytical instruments
subsystems.role: detects organic molecules and characterises minerals and isotopes.

subsystems.name: Mobility and chassis
subsystems.role: carries the drill and laboratory across rough terrain to chosen drill sites.
parts: six or more wheels with independent steering

subsystems.name: Navigation and subsurface sensing
subsystems.role: decides where to drive and where to drill, largely without help from Earth.

subsystems.name: Thermal and power
subsystems.role: keeps electronics alive through Martian nights and manages heat from the drill.

subsystems.name: Communications and lander interface
subsystems.role: relays commands and data and provides the descent and landing platform.
parts: UHF relay radio to an orbiter

buildSteps.title: Design the rover and its instrument suite
buildSteps.detail: Engineers fix the mass, power and volume budget across a drill, a sealed laboratory and a mobility system that all have to fit inside a single lander.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the structure and mobility system
buildSteps.detail: The chassis and suspension are built and the wheels and drive motors mated to it.

buildSteps.title: Build the drill
buildSteps.detail: A rotary-percussive mechanism, proven on Earth in Mars-analogue rock, is assembled so it can extract and retain a core for transfer.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the analytical laboratory
buildSteps.detail: The sealed sample path — mill, ovens and instrument inlet — is assembled and cleaned to remove terrestrial organic contamination.

buildSteps.title: Assemble instruments
buildSteps.detail: Each spectrometer and camera is built, calibrated against known reference materials and mounted on the rover.

buildSteps.title: Environmental testing
buildSteps.detail: The rover goes through thermal-vacuum, vibration and acoustic testing that simulates launch and the Martian surface; the drill is rehearsed in a low-pressure chamber.

buildSteps.title: Build the lander and descent system
buildSteps.detail: A European landing platform, parachutes and retro-rockets are assembled and qualified for the thin Martian atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Launch, cruise and land
buildSteps.detail: The rover would fly on a launcher arranged with a partner agency, coast to Mars and touch down at Oxia Planum, a clay-rich plain.

buildSteps.title: Drill and analyse
buildSteps.detail: The rover drives to targets picked from orbit and from its own ground-penetrating radar, drills a core, powders it and delivers it to the sealed instruments for a result sent back over the relay link.

prerequisites.why: a 2 m drill has been built and tested on Earth in Mars-like rock, but no rover has drilled that deeply on Mars.
organic molecules at part-per-billion levels are easy to fake with contamination from the spacecraft itself, so every surface must be cleaned and verified.

prerequisites.tech: Raman and mass spectrometry miniaturised for space
prerequisites.why: flight versions of these instruments have already operated on Mars.
driving and target selection without human real-time control has been demonstrated by earlier rovers.

prerequisites.tech: Entry, descent and landing in the thin atmosphere
prerequisites.why: large parachutes plus powered descent are a solved, if difficult, problem for medium-sized rovers.
solar arrays with radioisotope heaters have sustained rovers through many Martian winters.

pathway.milestone: rover assembled and tested, awaiting a launch opportunity; originally planned for 2022, now targeted at 2028
launch and landing on the clay-rich plain at Oxia Planum
pathway.unlocks: access to ancient sediments most likely to hold preserved organic matter.

pathway.milestone: first deep cores analysed inside a sealed laboratory on Mars
pathway.unlocks: a decisive test of whether complex organic chemistry survived below the oxidised surface.

pathway.milestone: sample return and precursor work for human missions
pathway.unlocks: laboratory-grade analysis on Earth and knowledge of subsurface resources and hazards.
